learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer, basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
The student will be able to differentiate between the different approaches to thermodynamic study.
Explain the laws of Thermodynamics in their own words.
Represent the property diagrams of pure substances.
Know the existing alternatives for calculating the thermodynamic properties of substances.
Analyze the operation of power generation thermal machines.
Analyze the operation of refrigeration and heat pump thermal machines.
Formulate the First Law for closed systems.
Calculate the variation of properties between the inlet and outlet of a control volume.
Demonstrate the equivalence of Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements.
Draw processes in the T-s property diagram.
Describe the scheme of a steam power cycle.
Use the Mollier diagram for calculating enthalpies in the superheated vapor region.
Represent the Brayton cycle in an h-s and p-v diagram.
Give an opinion on the social, economic, and environmental problems associated with power generation in thermal power plants.

syllabus_topics: UD 2. The First Law of Thermodynamics. Closed Systems
UD 4. The First Law of Thermodynamics. Control Volumes
UD 5. The Second Law of Thermodynamics
UD 7. Power Cycles for Work Production. Steam Turbines
UD 8. Gas Power Cycles. Gas Turbines
assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 4.0 in the final problem exam is required to average with laboratory practices and thematic seminars. Students can opt for a global exam, which entails a weighting of 80% for the final problem exam (minimum 4.0) and 20% for an additional written exam covering laboratory practices and thematic seminars. The grade obtained in the additional exam will be the final grade for practices and seminars, replacing any previous qualification. The final problem exam consists of 4 independent blocks, each with one problem, lasting 45 minutes, for a total of 3 hours.
